children: Eli Lilly (LLY) edged 1% higher in morning Tuesday trading after new data pointed to greater weight and blood-sugar reductions from its oral Foundayo treatment than oral semaglutide at higher doses.

The analysis examined 17.2 mg of Foundayo, or orforglipron, in adults with type 2 diabetes. At week 52, patients receiving the Lilly drug recorded 1.5% more body-weight reduction than those taking 25 mg of oral semaglutide.
The blood-sugar measure A1C also moved in Lilly's favor, with the analysis showing a further 0.3% reduction compared with the semaglutide group.

The findings were presented during the European Association for the Study of Diabetes meeting in Milan. Lilly has been developing Foundayo across its diabetes program as competition in oral GLP-1 medicines expands, with EASD materials listing additional studies involving the treatment.

The latest figures add another data point for investors tracking whether Foundayo can gain traction in the growing oral GLP-1 market among patients with type 2 diabetes. The comparison, however, comes from separate studies rather than a direct head-to-head trial.

title: Eli Lilly Shares Rise After Foundayo Shows More Weight Loss
